subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is a leitmotif in film music?
options: A recurring musical theme associated with a character, place, object or idea
A single sustained note held under a scene
Music that a character can hear within the film's world
The loudest section of a film score
questions.explain: A leitmotif is a short, memorable theme that returns each time its associated character or idea appears.

questions.q: What is 'underscore' in a film soundtrack?
options: Music played quietly beneath dialogue or action to support the scene
A theme sung by the on-screen characters
The end-credits song
A sudden loud musical accent
questions.explain: Underscore is background music that supports the mood of a scene without distracting from the dialogue or action.

questions.q: Which composer wrote the well-known scores for Jaws and Star Wars?
options: John Williams
Hans Zimmer
Ennio Morricone
Bernard Herrmann
questions.explain: John Williams composed the iconic scores for Jaws (1975) and Star Wars (1977).

questions.q: In Star Wars, 'The Imperial March' is the leitmotif for which character?
options: Darth Vader
Luke Skywalker
Princess Leia
Yoda
questions.explain: The stern, minor-key 'Imperial March' recurs as Darth Vader's leitmotif.

questions.q: What is a 'click track' used for in film-music recording?
options: To keep the performers precisely in time with the film's timing
To add reverb to the recording
To remove background noise
To sample real instruments
questions.explain: A click track is a metronomic guide that helps musicians synchronise the music exactly to the on-screen action.

questions.q: Which tonality is most commonly used to suggest sadness, tension or danger?
options: Minor key
Major key
Whole-tone scale
Pentatonic scale
questions.explain: A minor key is conventionally associated with sad, tense or threatening moods.

questions.q: Bernard Herrmann's score for Psycho (1960) is famously played by which instrument family only?
options: Strings
Brass
Woodwind
Percussion
questions.explain: Herrmann scored Psycho for a string orchestra alone, producing its stark, unsettling sound.

questions.q: Which term describes music synchronised exactly to on-screen movement, such as footsteps matched by staccato notes?
options: Mickey-mousing
Underscoring
Diegesis
Sampling
questions.explain: Mickey-mousing is when the music mirrors the on-screen action moment by moment.

questions.q: Why might a composer use tremolo strings in a suspense scene?
options: To build tension and a sense of unease
To create a calm, relaxed atmosphere
To signal a happy resolution
To imitate a marching rhythm
questions.explain: The shimmering, restless sound of tremolo strings heightens suspense and anxiety.

questions.q: What is the main dramatic purpose of using leitmotifs across a film?
options: To help the audience associate recurring themes with characters or ideas and follow the narrative
To make the score longer
To ensure every scene uses the same tempo
To replace the need for dialogue
questions.explain: Recurring leitmotifs reinforce characters and ideas, giving the score narrative unity.

questions.q: Why are synthesizers and electronic sounds often chosen for science-fiction films?
options: They can create futuristic, otherworldly timbres not available from acoustic instruments
They are always cheaper than any orchestra
They cannot play in a minor key
They remove the need for a click track
questions.explain: Electronic timbres evoke the alien and futuristic, suiting sci-fi settings.

questions.q: What is the usual effect of a low, sustained pedal note under a scene?
options: It builds tension and a sense of foreboding
It creates a light, cheerful mood
It signals the end of the film
It imitates birdsong
questions.explain: A held low pedal note creates underlying tension and anticipation.

questions.q: How does dissonance typically affect the mood of a horror scene?
options: It creates a feeling of unease and fear
It produces a warm, comforting mood
It makes the scene feel romantic
It suggests calm resolution
questions.explain: Clashing, dissonant harmonies unsettle the listener and heighten fear.

questions.q: What does it mean if film music is described as 'non-diegetic'?
options: It is heard by the audience but not by the characters on screen
It is sung live by the actors
It comes from a radio shown in the scene
It is played only during the credits
questions.explain: Non-diegetic music is score added for the audience; the characters cannot hear it.

questions.q: Why does synchronising music to picture matter when scoring a film?
options: So musical events align with the emotion and timing of the action on screen
So the film can be shown without any dialogue
So the orchestra can play faster
So the music can ignore the visuals
questions.explain: Careful synchronisation ensures musical hits and moods match the visual action precisely.

questions.q: What mood is usually created by a fast tempo combined with a driving ostinato in a chase scene?
options: Excitement and urgency
Peaceful calm
Deep sadness
Romantic tenderness
questions.explain: A quick tempo and repeated ostinato pattern drive energy and a sense of urgency.

questions.q: A director wants gentle music for a peaceful sunrise. Which combination best fits?
options: Slow tempo, major key, soft dynamics and warm strings
Fast tempo, minor key, loud brass and heavy percussion
Dissonant chords with sudden accents
A driving ostinato with tremolo strings
questions.explain: Slow, soft, major-key music with warm strings suits a calm, peaceful scene.

questions.q: A composer wants the audience to instantly recognise a hero every time they appear. Which technique is most appropriate?
options: Give the hero a distinctive recurring leitmotif
Use silence whenever the hero appears
Change the music style completely each time
Play the end-credits song under every entrance
questions.explain: A recurring leitmotif lets the audience identify the hero the moment their theme returns.

questions.q: A scene shows a strange alien landscape and the director wants an unearthly sound. Which resource is most suitable?
options: Synthesizers and electronic/sampled sounds
A solo acoustic guitar
A brass fanfare
A harpsichord playing a dance
questions.explain: Electronic and synthesized timbres readily suggest strange, otherworldly environments.

questions.q: To build suspense in the moments before a monster is revealed, which approach works best?
options: Quiet tremolo strings with a gradual crescendo towards the reveal
A cheerful major-key melody at a steady volume
A single loud chord followed by silence for the whole build-up
A slow lullaby in a warm major key
questions.explain: A quiet, restless build with a rising crescendo maximises tension before the reveal.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) Music (J536) specification; Area of Study 4: Film Music
